issues.legal_issue: An eviction appeal may be resolved by setting aside the eviction order and dismissing the eviction application when the tenant agrees to an enhanced rent.
material_facts: The premises had been leased for residential use but were being used commercially.
The court considered the location, rental rates for comparable premises, and the commercial use in proposing an enhanced rent.
The tenant agreed to the proposed monthly rent increase, effective from October 1, 1986.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, the eviction order was set aside, and the eviction application was dismissed; the landlord was entitled to the enhanced rent from the agreed effective date.
issues.legal_principle: The Court resolved the appeal on the basis of the tenant’s agreement to enhanced rent, taking account of the property’s location, comparable local rents, and its commercial use.

predicates.eviction_appeal: The tenant challenged an order directing eviction in an appeal.
predicates.tenant_accepted_rent_increase: The tenant agreed to pay rent at an increased rate.

issues.definition: When a tenant appealing an eviction order agrees to an increased rent, the eviction order is set aside and the eviction application is dismissed.

issues.legal_issue: A departure from the use permitted by a lease may be permitted while a penalty for the wrongful use is paid.
material_facts: The premises were leased for residential use but were put to commercial use.
The development authority objected to the change of use and proceeded to raise a penalty.
The Court relied on a High Court decision concerning a similar change of use and directed the Controller to quantify the penalty after hearing the parties and the development authority.
issues.conclusion: The Controller was directed to fix the penalty after hearing the relevant parties, and the tenant was liable to pay it; the deviation in use could be permitted while the penalty continued to be paid.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 14(1)(k) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, the Court followed Daljit Singh Madan v. Surinder Kumar, which held that the Controller could fix a penalty for wrongful use and that the departure from the permitted use could be allowed while the penalty continued to be paid.

predicates.eviction_proceeding_for_change_of_use: An eviction proceeding was brought because the tenant used the premises for a purpose different from the permitted purpose.
predicates.lease_purpose_differs_from_actual_use: The tenant used the premises for a purpose different from the purpose for which they were leased.
predicates.penalty_paid: The tenant continued to pay the penalty imposed for the wrongful use.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding concerns a tenant’s use of premises for a purpose different from the permitted purpose, and the tenant pays the penalty for that use, the changed use may be permitted while the penalty continues to be paid.
